chunks: Al-Hasan ibn 'Abdillah ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa narrated to me from his father 'Abdillah ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from 'Abdillah ibn Waddah, from 'Abdillah ibn Shu'ayb Al-Tamimi, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

On the Day of Judgment, a caller will call out, 'Where are the Shia of the family of Muhammad?' A group of people whose number cannot be counted except by Allah, the Exalted, will stand up and move aside from (the rest of) the people. Then a caller will call out, 'Where are the Zuwwar of the grave of Husayn (peace be upon him)?' A large group of people will stand up. They will be told, 'Take the hand of whomever you like and take them along (with you) to Paradise.' They will take whomever they like (to Paradise) to such an extent that a person will say to one of them, 'O so-and-so! Do you not remember me?! I stood up for you once (as an act of respect).' Therefore, the man will take him to Paradise without being stopped.

key_terms.زُوَّارُ قَبْرِ الْحُسَيْنِ: Visitors of the grave of Husayn
key_terms.شِيعَةُ آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ: Shia of the family of Muhammad

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for visiting the grave of Imam Husayn on the Day of Judgment?
ai.summary: In Kamil al-Ziyarat, Ibn Qulawayh records this narration highlighting the unique status of Ziyarat al-Husayn as a means of securing intercession and communal salvation. The scene depicts a divine call distinguishing the 'Shia of the Ahl al-Bayt' and specifically the 'visitors of Husayn’s grave,' granting them the authority to select companions for Paradise, thereby emphasizing the social and spiritual bonds forged through pilgrimage. This reflects the Shia scholarly view that ziyarah is not merely ritualistic but a transformative act that establishes networks of mutual support and divine favor on the Day of Judgment.
